attribution.new_contribution: Original Lean formalization by Levent Alpöge. The unchanged FractionalSliceDomains proof is Fortytwo’s native edit. Codex contributed the following additional reductions. The signed orthonormal coordinate majorant applies to every coordinate vector and the flag law transports it to related frames. Use the common orthonormal signed-frame majorant formula to bound the coordinate operator norm. The stored matrix columns give the standard orthonormal expansion. Use an orthonormal frame for the flag. The Hermitian form is the signed sum of the coordinate norms, and the majorant is their unsigned sum, so the triangle inequality gives the bound. Evaluate the Hermitian self-pairing by the diagonal Gram formula for the orthonormal frame and split its signature by coordinate block. Use positivity of the Hermitian dot product, injectivity of the embedding and linearity of the majorant covector for the unipotent projection. The Euclidean linear map represented by the matrix is continuous in finite dimension, so its operator norm uniformly bounds every nonzero vector’s norm quotient. Replace the explicit signed Gram–Schmidt recursion with orthonormal bases on the positive and sign-reversed negative definite subspaces. Their original cross orthogonality and spanning property retain every required coordinate. Use one symmetric trace pairing on each argument, transport linear independence through the inverse coordinate map, and reuse the Fourier-frequency coordinate equivalence. Regard the integral pairing on the discrete lattice as an additive integer-valued character, and use the kernel of its continuous inner-product functional to extend orthogonality from the lattice to its span. A matrix congruent to the identity preserves the lattice; use the same argument for the unipotent inverse and the existing Hermitian linearity to show period invariance. Evaluate the real character on a trace-dual basis and use linear independence of Galois embeddings to identify every complex coefficient. Projecting two vectors orthogonal to the isotropic line preserves their Hermitian pairing; prove this once for the lifted functional and its later alternating trace. The alternating trace form uses the same projected Hermitian pairing as the coordinate functional in the unipotent action. Extend the annihilating real-linear relation to the conjugation-fixed subfield by clearing one denominator for each element, then apply field-character independence without the auxiliary integral submonoid.
